A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LAT research, with matching authors, methods, and experimental applications. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite the shortened title and revised presentation.

before.justification: V1 reports original jailbreak-defense, backdoor-removal, and unlearning experiments in Tables 2–5, with additional empirical analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and reports additional jailbreak evaluations, including the targeted-versus-untargeted comparison in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A.1 change Llama3 training from interleaved benign supervised fine-tuning to KL regularization against the frozen original model on UltraChat. Llama2 retains supervised fine-tuning, and the principal LAT attack and defense procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Jailbreak test coverage expands from five attack types to six through PAIR, reported under both autograders. The training corpora, backdoor scenarios, Harry Potter evaluations, and WMDP tasks are retained. Llama3 was already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: New Appendix B/Table 6 evaluates untargeted RT-EAT-LAT against refusal training and targeted RT-EAT-LAT. The existing R2D2, RT-EAT, DPO, WHP, GA, and RMU comparison methods are retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds PAIR testing and a targeted-versus-untargeted control experiment. The reported Llama3 training condition changes to KL regularization. Existing benchmark metrics, backdoor training settings, and WMDP relearning procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix B directly tests the central targetedness choice, a control absent from v1. Table 6 reports untargeted versus targeted prefill attack success of 0.375 versus 0.068 and GCG success of 0.076 versus 0.009. V2 also adds a manual jailbreak case and qualitative autograder error analysis; earlier supplementary analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V1 Table 2 explicitly reports single-model Llama3 results, while v2 reports means and standard errors across three random seeds. Three-seed reporting already existed for trained Llama2 models, and the backdoor and unlearning reporting practices are retained.

E6.justification: V2 adds PAIR columns and untargeted-LAT results and replaces the trained Llama3 result rows alongside the changed loss and run reporting. For example, RT-EAT-LAT MT-Bench changes from 0.787 to 0.829. Backdoor and unlearning table values are retained. V2 inconsistently reports uncertainty for the same Llama3 MMLU mean of 0.613: ±0.009 in Table 2 versus ±0.016 in Table 7.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds a mathematical definition of frozen-reference KL benign regularization in Equation 7, extending the previous SFT-only formulation. The other substantive loss equations are retained; their renumbering and added explanatory underbraces do not constitute theoretical changes.

C1.justification: The abstract and enumerated contributions retain the same core claims: targeted LAT improves jailbreak robustness, trigger-unknown backdoor removal, and robust unlearning with limited general-capability tradeoffs. The shorter title and expanded discussion do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds qualifications about successful manual jailbreaks and potentially substantial StrongReject false positives, and explicitly states that removal of harmful circuitry remains unconfirmed. It also adds interpretations concerning KL-based capability retention, targetedness tradeoffs, and generalization from WMDP training documents to multiple-choice evaluations.

D1.justification: V2 documents a practical heuristic of perturbing four approximately evenly spaced layers, clarifies that refusal-string matching applies only to benign compliance, and adds a research-demo access link. These disclosures do not establish changes to the retained experiments' specified attack layers.

R1.justification: V2 adds five cited works and removes three. Most notably, it acknowledges Zeng et al.'s BEEAR as concurrent targeted LAT for backdoor removal, qualifying the contrast with prior work. Discussion of related latent-manipulation techniques and rigorous evaluations also expands.

P1.justification: V2 shortens the title, edits introductory and experimental prose, expands selected explanations, and corrects Appendix A.1's heading from R2D2-LAT to RT-LAT. A new Appendix B shifts subsequent appendix labels, while the overall narrative and section organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The result graphics accompanying Tables 2, 4, and 5 change from normalized radar plots to bar plots with explicit scales and error bars. Table 3's chart separates general and robust performance. V2 also adds PAIR columns and an ablation table, revises captions and legends, and corrects attack-success direction arrows.

improvement.justification: V2 adds a direct targeted-versus-untargeted control on Llama3 and three-seed reporting, strengthening support for a key method choice. Additional attack coverage, explicit evaluator and mechanistic limitations, and clearer result graphics improve the paper. These gains outweigh limited reporting problems, including unexplained uncertainty discrepancies between Tables 2 and 7.
